name: Cycles of last digits
formula: \text{units digit of } a^n \text{ repeats with period } 1, 2 \text{ or } 4: \quad 2\!:\ 2,4,8,6 \quad 3\!:\ 3,9,7,1 \quad 7\!:\ 7,9,3,1 \quad 8\!:\ 8,4,2,6
whenToUse: The units digit (or the remainder mod a small number) of a big power. List a few powers, find the period, reduce the exponent.
example: The units digit of $7^{2026}$: powers of $7$ end in $7, 9, 3, 1$ and repeat every $4$. Since $2026 \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, the units digit is the second in the cycle, $9$.
pitfall: An exponent that is a multiple of $4$ gives the LAST entry of the cycle, not the first. Only the units digit of the base matters.
